### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d450005a06e7d1c4794ea0d926567ff6b02f90b8` — the merge of head `a12ff6bd8835bf887ece378b577d235776e1133d` into base `bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d450005a06e7d1c4794ea0d926567ff6b02f90b8 && git checkout d450005a06e7d1c4794ea0d926567ff6b02f90b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d a12ff6bd8835bf887ece378b577d235776e1133d && git checkout -B drift-repro bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d && git merge --no-ff a12ff6bd8835bf887ece378b577d235776e1133d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bd4276a91e94d6edf803110ccea4ca6bcbbf810d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**Every door `record:json` was accepted at is now a refusal, each judged right.**

- **The enum.** `record:json` leaves `PageComponentType.options`; the enum's own error map (`page.zod.ts`: an `error` callback that looks `issue.input` up in `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES`) answers the retired name with the prescription as `invalid_value`, and a stranger (`record:jsonl`) keeps zod's own message. Keeping the row is required, not optional: `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES` derives from the row keys, lint's props gate skips a rowless type as an unregistered custom string, and `check-yaml-examples` judges only rowed types. Right.
- **`PageSchema` at the element path.** Refused at `regions[0].components[1].type`, one `custom` issue, with the same page parsing when `record:approvals` sits in that slot. Right.
- **The lint door.** `validate-component-types.ts` reads the map: `component-type-unknown` at `…type` as `error`, message = `retiredTypeHead(prescription)` ("`record:json` was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0049)") plus the fixed relay clause, hint = `retiredTypeRemedy(prescription)` = "Delete the `record:json` component node and put nothing in its place". `component-props-invalid` at `…properties` for every bag, `{}` included, because the row is `z.never`. The typo suggester drops the name without an edit: `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPE_CANDIDATES` is `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES` minus `RETIRED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES`. Right.
- **The prescription against the playbook's §2 conventions.** Backticked fully qualified name first (`record:json`, the spelling the `ai:chat_window` and `user:profile` entries use for a component type); "was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 (ADR-0049)" — 18 is the right version, the type was published in `18.0.0-next.3` only and the removal ships on the 18 line; a dash clause stating why (declared for one panel, the panel was dropped, no renderer, no placement, the three props configure nothing); the imperative fix "Delete the `record:json` component node and put nothing in its place."; no `os migrate meta` sentence, which is right because no conversion covers the surface (the `retired-key-migrate-sentence` class pin requires the house sentence only where a prescription names the command); no tracker number, pinned by the test's `ISSUE_ID` regex. Right.

**Nothing else's accept set moves, judged right.**

- `PRINT_REFUSED_PAGE_COMPONENT_TYPES` loses its `record:json` row. Required by that map's own docblock ("The retired types are refused by name at the parse already and are not repeated here") and by `page-print.test.ts`, whose census takes `KNOWN_COMPONENT_TYPES` minus the retired map and reports a retired key in either print set as stale — leaving the row would have gone red. `validate-print-page-blocks.ts` already skips retired types. Right.
- The open string arm stays open: `custom.record_json`, `object-grid`, `record:details` pinned parsing. Right.
- The four record blocks' fail-open `requiredPermissions` are byte-identical; the field-security census pin moves from five declarers to four, and the 23134 whole-bag set gains `record:json` (a `z.never` row refuses the key as `invalid_type`, not `unrecognized_keys`). Right.
- Strictness-ledger counts `ui/` 214 → 213 and `component.zod.ts` 81 → 80: exactly one `strictObject(` site left. Right.

**`RecordJsonProps` leaves the public surface completely, and the ratchets move as a whole-def deletion must.** The const and the type are deleted from `component.zod.ts`; the `ui` barrel is `export *` only (no named re-export existed at the merge base); `api-surface/ui.json` −2 (const, type), `declaration-map/ui.json` −1, `export-origins/ui.json` −1, `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` −1 (`ui/RecordJsonProps`), `authorable-surface/ui.json` −3 (`field`, `label`, `requiredPermissions`). **No D2 conversion — right under the playbook's §3.** §3's conversion is a per-key `stripKeys`. Here the whole element leaves and its row is `z.never`, so a strip would list three mechanical edits whose result, a bare node, the parse refuses by name anyway — the author must delete the node regardless, and the tool would be listing edits the author then undoes. `conversions/registry.ts`'s `element-filter-removed` docblock states the rule the PR cites: "The component node itself is NOT removed: deleting authored page nodes is a layout decision a mechanical conversion must not make."
